headline: GlowberryClient BETA3 — Module Data Fixes, Blueberry UI & Native Route Cleanup
summary: The module catalogue entries that were disabled, or enabled but doing nothing, purely because they were refused for lack of a live native game feed now work wherever this build actually has a route to their data. Every entry is classified by the route it needs, and only the entries that genuinely require a feed this build does not expose stay badged, with the reason they are badged.

sections.title: Module Catalogue — Phase A: device input and launcher state (no game data needed)

items.text: HUD readouts: clock, keystrokes, memory, watermark, combo, death counter, K/D tracker, streak tracker, kill counter.
Actions: drop all, chat macro, command bind, auto GG, auto tip.
Input-driven cooldown readouts: attack cooldown, attack indicator, crit timer, pearl timer, gapple timer, shield timer, hit marker.
Sprint helpers: no sprint reset, sprint swing, keep sprint.

sections.title: Module Catalogue — Phase B: the game options file

items.text: Bob off, fullbright (self and world), particle off, sprint particles, FOV boost. Each writes the instance's options file, applied on the next game load.

sections.title: Module Catalogue — Phase C: the local-player feed

items.text: Coordinates, direction, compass, chunk borders, speedometer, health display, position display, speed display, velocity display, fall damage warning, waypoints, death waypoint.

sections.title: Module Catalogue — Phase D: the peer feed

items.text: Reach circle, target HUD and target info, from the proximity-voice peer feed (needs no game hook).

sections.title: Module Catalogue — Phases E and F: honestly badged, not faked

items.text: Engine/render hooks are not reachable on the shipped builds: the game exposes no entity, block, inventory or effect feed to a mod. These stay badged with the reason, instead of showing a fabricated reading.
Server-decided or ban-risk behaviour (reach, knockback, crits, TPS, inventory automation) is not shipped on purpose and is badged with the note that says which.
Retired the raw OpenGL ES mesh rasteriser, which cannot draw on a Vulkan-only RenderDragon build, along with its draw self-test cube and mesh draw counter.
Capes reach the game through the engine's own texture loader, so a cape appears with no resource pack, no world reload and no GL renderer.
Accessories and pets reach the game through the client's native player-render hook; where that hook is not live the panel says the piece is preview-only instead of implying it is drawn.

Cosmetics diagnostics now report the route that is actually live (cape engine texture route, engine image pipeline, player-render hook) and name the first failing stage, rather than a GLES draw count.

sections.title: Also in this release (everything since OV.2)

items.text: Cosmetics: capes, pets and hats reach the game across versions; native render pipeline, authored Blockbench mesh support, per-piece textures and the in-app cosmetics diagnostics.
Cosmetics plan phases 0-6: rules revision and version coverage, honest skin identity, the cape engine texture swap, hand-designed capes, pet asset measurement and the big-server skin finding.

Plan phases 7-13: a real F3-style debug readout, Closet icon sections with standalone previews, the replay transport, an alphabetised Mod Menu, the Launch tab revamp, a controller cursor with connection toasts, and every emoji icon removed.
Software rasteriser preview (character, pet, cape, accessories) with golden-image tests.
Blueberry UI: shared design tokens and a component library, restyled Mod Menus, radial wheel, Closet and Launch tab; blue is the default accent.
Real Minecraft skin shown from the engine-hook seam, with the XUID-based account skin resolver enabled after a Microsoft sign-in.
FPS modules trimmed to the seven options that work; the radial hub head follows the cursor; the cursor disc is replaced with a clean pointer arrow.
Signature rules revision 7: fresh pause/HUD hooks for 1.26.30-1.26.52.
